title: Ryukyu Kingdom
capsule: The Ryukyu Kingdom was an island monarchy centered at Shuri Castle on Okinawa, unified in 1429 when Shō Hashi of Chūzan conquered Hokuzan and Nanzan and received the dynastic name 'Shō' from the Ming court. Under Shō Shin (r. 1477–1526) the kingdom reached its apex as a maritime entrepôt trading with China, Japan, Korea, Siam, Malacca, and Java. A Satsuma Domain invasion in 1609 reduced Ryukyu to a vassal of the Shimazu clan while it maintained nominal Qing tributary status; this dual dependency persisted until the Meiji government abolished the kingdom in 1879, proclaiming Okinawa Prefecture and exiling the last king Shō Tai to Tokyo.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's core territory on Okinawa is well attested; the precise extent of outer island dependencies and zones of Satsuma overlordship are less sharply defined in historical cartography.
